title: Check lists and text
summary: A length check and a containment check answer different questions about a list.
introduction: A length check and a containment check answer different questions about a list. We will use a small example so you can follow each step.
learningObjectives: Use the example to answer a practice question

blocks.text: A length check and a containment check answer different questions about a list.

blocks.code:
import { test, expect, jest, beforeEach } from "@jest/globals";
test("reading list", () => { const books = ["Moon", "Ocean"]; expect(books).toHaveLength(2); expect(books).toContain("Moon"); });
blocks.title: Check lists and text

blocks.text: Both checks pass: there are two books, and Moon is one of them.

items: Read the example from top to bottom. Point to the part that uses the new idea.
Add Zoo and update only the length expectation.
Explain what changed in your own words. Check the example again if you get stuck.

blocks.title: A common mistake
blocks.text: Having the right length does not prove the right values are present.
For more detail later, use this [Jest further reading](https://jestjs.io/docs/getting-started).
